subject.title: fix(auto-reply): preserve Unicode in treemap label sanitization and truncation

question: Should `/context map` gain supported Unicode label rendering, or should its current ASCII bitmap-font contract remain intentional?
rationale: The proposed patch cannot implement Unicode display without a renderer capable of painting those glyphs, and choosing that rendering scope is a product and implementation-direction decision.

options.title: Pause for Unicode rendering direction
options.body: Do not merge the partial allowlist change until an owner decides whether arbitrary Unicode labels are a supported `/context map` requirement.

options.title: Keep the ASCII renderer contract
options.body: Retain ASCII sanitization and close this branch because code-point truncation has no reachable Unicode input in the current render path.

options.title: Implement complete Unicode rendering
options.body: Adopt a Unicode-capable text-rendering path, preserve suitable label characters, and prove CJK and supplementary-character output in the rendered image.

recommendation.title: Pause for Unicode rendering direction
recommendation.body: Do not merge the partial allowlist change until an owner decides whether arbitrary Unicode labels are a supported `/context map` requirement.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and merged the current context-map renderer and are best positioned to confirm its intended glyph and dependency boundary.
